title.narrative: Food Assistance in South Lubero, North Kivu

description.narrative: The ongoing armed violence in northern Rutshuru and southern Lubero territories continues to expose thousands of Congolese, including women and children, to extremely difficult living conditions. Since the M23's advances in late June 2024, approximately 300,000 displaced have been affected in Lubero, with over 92,565 returnees in Lubero since March 2024. The M23's control of key towns in southern Lubero has led to significant population movements, exacerbating the humanitarian situation. Many displaced individuals have returned to areas (health zones of South Lubero) where basic infrastructure has been destroyed. Also, the June 2024 harvest, below average in conflict zones due to reductions in cultivated areas, did not significantly improve food consumption among poor households. Area-level Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected, with a proportion of displaced households in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) until January 2025.The food security and protection crises in the DRC are deeply intertwined. Among displaced women and girls in Goma, approximately 1 in 10 were raped. Poor living conditions push displaced women and girls into survival sex and expose them to risks of sexual exploitation. Providing regular and predictable levels of basic assistance designed in a gender-sensitive way can mitigate the GBV crisis by reducing negative coping strategies. To meet urgent food needs and prevent a deterioration in food security, WFP will provide three months emergency food assistance to 25,119 vulnerable displaced people in spontaneous settlements and host communities around Kayna and Kanyabayonga in Lubero, where the crisis has intensified in recent weeks and where there is a critical food need. However, given the unpredictable security situation, with the movements of armed groups and the intensification of attacks reducing humanitarian access the principle of flexibility at territorial level remains important, to monitor the movements of IDPs in line with humanitarian access. Given that the purchase of food will take between 3 and 4 months, WFP will use the stocks available on flexible grants to begin distributions from the 2nd month. Once the foodstuffs have been purchased, they will replace those already borrowed from stocks.
